messages:
lily_ae: Heads up
Client: MiraCorp. POC blocked by their security team 
—they require certificate-based auth or proof of TLS client validation. They're refusing pure IP allowlist. Any quick options?

ryan_se: TL;DR: Dedicated can provide static egress IPs quickly. We don't advertise mTLS client-auth for hosted/dedicated endpoints by default. For a short POC we have two pragmatic approaches: 1) reserve static NAT IPs and combine with other controls, or 2) temporary client-cert pinning at the gateway (manual + exception).

mira-netops: Procurement won't spin up a proxy. They want to hand over a small set of firewall rules and be done. Would prefer client certs if possible.

morgan_infra: We can reserve two /32 NAT IPs for a Dedicated pool in the next 4 hours. If Security approves, infra can manually configure the edge to require and validate a pinned client cert fingerprint for the duration of the POC. That is a manual change and not standard.

sam_security: Security: client-cert pinning is allowed for POC with constraints: - cert TTL <= 7 days, - customer-generated CSR preferred, - documented issuance/revocation, - signed exception form. We'll need SEC-POC-88 created and an audit entry.

lily_ae: Can we get a copy-paste allowlist and a curl example for the cert flow to give to MiraCorp? They want exact bits to drop into their ticket.

ryan_se: Sure. Allowlist snippet (send to their firewall team):

```
# MiraCorp - Redwood Dedicated POC allowlist
198.51.100.45/32  # nat egress ip A
198.51.100.46/32  # nat egress ip B
# destination: dedicated-mira.pool.redwood.ai (443)
```

ryan_se: curl sample for client cert test (assumes we enable pinning):

```
curl --cacert redwood-ca.pem \
  --cert mira-client.pem --key mira-client.key \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DEDICATED-API-KEY>" \
  https://dedicated-mira.pool.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

morgan_infra: I'll open INF-5050 to reserve the IPs and note the manual TLS change if Security signs off.

sam_security: I'll draft the quick exception and revocation playbook (SEC-POC-88). Steps we'll require: 1) customer produces CSR or requests template; 2) Redwood issues short-lived cert OR accepts customer cert fingerprint; 3) infra pins fingerprint and enable check; 4) perform connectivity test; 5) rotate or revoke and remove pin at POC end.

mira-netops: CSR preferred. Can you provide the CSR template with exact CN/SAN expectations?

ryan_se: CSR guidance: CN=mira-poc-client, SAN=email:mira-poc@miracorp.com (optional), key: ECDSA P-256 or RSA2048. Provide PEM-encoded CSR over SFTP or our secure portal.

lily_ae: What about logs? They want proof that client auth succeeded. Can we provide that without leaking connection detail?

sam_security: We can provide a signed audit extract with timestamps of auth success/failure for the POC window. Not raw packet captures. That should satisfy compliance for a week-long eval.

morgan_infra: Action items: INF-5050 (reserve 198.51.100.45 & .46), SEC-POC-88 draft, AE to request CSR or confirm Redwood-issued cert. I'll update ticket when NAT IPs are live.

deploy-bot: [ticket] INF-5050 created by morgan_infra - reserved nat 198.51.100.45, 198.51.100.46

lily_ae: Great. I'll ask MiraCorp to produce a CSR and I'll send them the allowlist + curl example. Call scheduled 2025-11-12 10:00 PT to finalize. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
